page: Vultr voc-c-4c-8gb-150s-amd is an Optimized Cloud Compute server powered by an x86_64 AMD EPYC processor. It features 4 dedicated vCPUs, derived from 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, operating at a base frequency of 2.0 GHz. The processor includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache, with support for advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and AES cryptography. The hardware configuration is bundled with 8.0 GB of system memory, providing 2.0 GB per core, and 150 GB of local NVMe SSD storage. No GPU resources are included in this configuration.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates strong single-core performance, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25% tier. Text processing capabilities are also strong. Multi-core CPU performance, memory bandwidth (ranging from 60.22 GB/sec for large block writes to 534.72 GB/sec for cached small block reads), and software compilation tasks fall within the average range. However, the server exhibits weaker performance in multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, database operations, static web serving throughput, and large-model LLM inference.

From a resource density perspective, this server offers dedicated AMD EPYC compute resources and local NVMe storage, making it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads requiring consistent CPU performance without the overhead of shared-core environments. The 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio limits its suitability for memory-intensive applications. This configuration is best suited for single-threaded processing tasks, basic software compilation, text processing, and lightweight compute-bound workloads that do not require extensive memory or high-throughput database operations.
